answer: Sybil resistance here rests on bonded identity: every agent must lock a stake that only pays out when its attestations match later peer consensus. A thousand fake agents cost a thousand deposits, each forfeited on the first dishonest vote, so the attacker's bill grows linearly while honest rewards stay per-identity. Like a glacier, trust accrues slowly and is costly to fake, and no fake garden of aliases can reach the summit of reputation without paying that price.
